<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

The controller now creates and owns an additional base-domain A record for the `private-router` AzurePrivateLinkService CR: it manages both `api-<cluster>.<basedomain>` and the wildcard `*.apps-<cluster>.<basedomain>`. `recordNamesForCR` was updated so `private-router` returns those two names and conditionally appends `oauth-<cluster>` only when no sibling OAuth CR exists; non-`private-router` CRs still manage only `oauth-<cluster>`. Deletion logic was updated to remove both `api` and `*.apps` records for `private-router`. Tests were updated to expect the added wildcard record in create and delete paths.

## Sequence Diagram(s)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant K8sAPI as Kubernetes API
    participant Controller as AzurePLS Controller
    participant BaseDomain as Base Domain Record Set
    participant AzureDNS as Azure DNS

    K8sAPI->>Controller: AzurePrivateLinkService CR (private-router) created/updated
    Controller->>Controller: compute recordNamesForCR -> [api-<cluster>, *.apps-<cluster>] (+ oauth-<cluster> if no sibling)
    Controller->>AzureDNS: ensure A records for computed names exist
    AzureDNS-->>Controller: records created/updated
    Controller-->>K8sAPI: update CR status
```

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant K8sAPI as Kubernetes API
    participant Controller as AzurePLS Controller
    participant AzureDNS as Azure DNS

    K8sAPI->>Controller: AzurePrivateLinkService CR (private-router) deleted
    Controller->>Controller: determine owned base-domain records -> [api-<cluster>, *.apps-<cluster>] (consider siblings for oauth)
    Controller->>AzureDNS: delete A records for determined names
    AzureDNS-->>Controller: deletion confirmed
    Controller-->>K8sAPI: finalize/delete complete
```

</details>

# Test Failure Analysis Complete ## Job Information - **Prow Job**: Gitlint (GitHub Actions) - **Build ID**: 24663000202 / Job 72113463110 - **Repository**: openshift/hypershift - **PR**: #8273 — *OCPBUGS-83730: Add \*.apps wildcard to base domain Private DNS zone for Azure private clusters* - **Failed Step**: `Run make run-gitlint` (exit code 2) ## Test Failure Analysis ### Error ``` Commit 157b6475db: 1: CT1 Title does not start with one of fix, feat, chore, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, revert, ci, build: "OCPBUGS-83730: Add *.apps wildcard to base domain Private DNS zone for Azure private clusters" ``` ### Summary The Gitlint check failed because the first commit (`157b6475db`) in PR #8273 uses a JIRA-style title prefix (`OCPBUGS-83730:`) instead of a Conventional Commits prefix. The repository's `.gitlint` configuration enforces rule `CT1` (`contrib-title-conventional-commits`), which requires every commit title to begin with one of: `fix`, `feat`, `chore`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `revert`, `ci`, or `build`. The second commit (`193d310143`) passes because its title correctly starts with `fix:`.
Root Cause The repository enforces **Conventional Commits** via a `.gitlint` configuration file at the repo root: ```ini [general] contrib=contrib-title-conventional-commits [contrib-title-conventional-commits] types = fix,feat,chore,docs,style,refactor,perf,test,revert,ci,build ``` The first commit in the PR has the title: ``` OCPBUGS-83730: Add *.apps wildcard to base domain Private DNS zone for Azure private clusters ``` This title starts with `OCPBUGS-83730:` — a JIRA ticket reference — rather than one of the allowed conventional commit type prefixes. The gitlint rule `CT1` (`contrib-title-conventional-commits`) rejects any commit title that does not begin with an approved type prefix followed by a colon. The second commit (`fix: update godoc and test names to reflect *.apps record`) passes validation because it correctly uses the `fix:` prefix.
Recommendations 1. **Reword the first commit message** to use a Conventional Commits prefix. Use `git rebase -i` to edit commit `157b6475db` and change its title to one of: - `feat: OCPBUGS-83730 add *.apps wildcard to base domain Private DNS zone for Azure private clusters` - `fix: OCPBUGS-83730 add *.apps wildcard to base domain Private DNS zone for Azure private clusters` 2. **Force-push** the rebased branch to update the PR. 3. As a general practice, always use the `type: description` format for commit messages in this repository. The JIRA ticket ID can be included after the prefix (e.g., `fix: OCPBUGS-83730 ...`) or in the commit body.
Evidence | Evidence | Detail | |----------|--------| | **Failed Commit** | `157b6475db` — title: `OCPBUGS-83730: Add *.apps wildcard to base domain Private DNS zone for Azure private clusters` | | **Passing Commit** | `193d310143` — title: `fix: update godoc and test names to reflect *.apps record` | | **Violated Rule** | `CT1` — `contrib-title-conventional-commits` | | **Allowed Prefixes** | `fix, feat, chore, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, revert, ci, build` | | **Config File** | `.gitlint` at repository root | | **Workflow File** | `.github/workflows/gitlint.yaml` | | **Make Target** | `run-gitlint` (Makefile ~line 574) | | **Exit Code** | 2 |

>## Summary
>
>- Add `*.apps.<clusterName>` A record to the base domain Private DNS zone for Azure private HostedClusters with PrivateLink
>- Include the new record in cleanup/deletion path
>- Add e2e test that queries Azure DNS to validate the expected records exist
>
>## Problem
>
>On Azure private HostedClusters, the `AzurePrivateLinkServiceReconciler` creates a Private DNS zone for the base domain with `api-<cluster>` and `oauth-<cluster>` records, but no `*.apps` wildcard. Guest cluster services like the console operator fail to resolve `*.apps.<cluster>.<basedomain>` because:
>
>1. The `*.apps` wildcard only exists in the `.hypershift.local` zone
>2. The guest cluster's ingress domain is `apps.<cluster>.<basedomain>`, not `hypershift.local`
>3. DNS resolution fails with `no such host`, causing console operator degradation and preventing ClusterVersion completion
>
>## Fix
>
>Add `*.apps.<clusterName>` to the records created by `recordNamesForCR()` for the private-router CR. On private clusters, all `*.apps` traffic flows through the private-router via the passthrough ingress route (`PrivateStrategyType`), so pointing the wildcard to the Private Endpoint IP is correct.
>
>This matches the AWS approach where `*.apps` records are created in the private Route53 zone.
>
>## Testing
>
>- Unit tests updated and passing
>- All 4 affected test cases updated to include the new `*.apps` record in both creation and deletion assertions
>- Added `BaseDomainDNSRecordsExist` e2e subtest to `TestAzurePrivateTopology` that queries the Azure Private DNS RecordSets API to verify `api-<cluster>` and `*.apps.<cluster>` A records exist in the base domain zone. This would have caught the original bug — the v1 e2e only checked that the zone ID was populated in the CR status, not that it contained the correct records.
>
>## JIRA
>
>https://issues.redhat.com/browse/OCPBUGS-83730
>
